title: P0: Rollout autoscaler cooldown mismatch -> streaming fragmentation postmortem
content:
Summary:

On 2029-06-12 at ~03:22 UTC we observed a P0 degradation of the Hosted API streaming surface: sustained stream fragmentation, reconnect storms, and elevated 5xx rates affecting ~14% of active streaming sessions for ~28 minutes. Customer-facing symptoms were partial responses (stream fragments aborted mid-token) and frequent client reconnects. No data exfiltration or integrity loss was detected.

Impact:
- Affected product: Hosted API streaming (chunked/HTTP2 & WebSocket proxies)
- User visible: truncated/aborted streams, increased reconnects, transient 5xx for streaming endpoints
- Scope: ~14% of concurrent streaming sessions globally; hit particularly hard in EU-west due to deployment topology
- Duration: ~28 minutes (03:22 UTC -> 03:50 UTC) until full mitigation; monitoring signals normalized by 04:05 UTC
- Business: several paid customers reported degraded UX; incident escalated to P0.

Timeline (condensed):
- 03:20 UTC: Canary rollout of autoscaler change (infra autoscaler v2.7.0) begins. Change includes: reduced cool-down floor and a new aggressive downscale path for low CPU + low token-per-second signals in order to reclaim GPUs during low token churn.
- 03:22 UTC: SRE alert — streaming-fragment-rate spikes in EU-west, p95 stream duration drops, reconnect rate increases.
- 03:25 UTC: First pager; oncall investigates dashboards, sees correlated decrease in ephemeral worker count and KV-cache lease churn alarms.
- 03:28 UTC: Observed rapid downscale events on nodes serving streaming sessions; multiplexed edge proxies lost session affinity; partial KV cache warming caused mid-stream KV misses.
- 03:31 UTC: Team rolls back canary to previous autoscaler config in EU-west. Rollback initiated via infra rollout job.
- 03:36 UTC: Partial relief — downscale events stop, but residual reconnect/backpressure patterns persist as KV cache reheating occurs and client multiplex windows reopen.
- 03:45 UTC: Emergency hotfix deployed to runtime to guard streaming sessions against immediate eviction during downscale (short term patch: respect 'stream-in-flight' flag).
- 03:50 UTC: Streaming fragmentation metric returns near baseline; monitoring continues.
- 04:05 UTC: All dependent telemetry stabilized. Post-incident conference call started at ~05:00 UTC for timeline and action planning.

Root cause:
Primary cause: A configuration change in autoscaler v2.7.0 reduced the effective cooldown/hysteresis for downscale decisions and introduced a new combined signal (low CPU AND low tokens-per-second) that triggered mass downscales even while active streaming sessions had high KV cache dependency and multiplexed session affinity. The new downscale path did not account for the 'stream-in-flight' annotation produced by the serving runtime; as a result nodes hosting in-progress streaming sessions were deprovisioned or had worker processes terminated mid-stream.

Contributing factors:
- Canary scope and canary traffic shaping were insufficiently conservative for autoscaler changes that affect node lifecycle. Canary targeted a small percentage of API traffic but not specifically streaming-dominant shards.
- Lack of a runtime-exported deploy-time guard: the autoscaler relied only on CPU/TPS signals and not the 'stream-in-flight' metric; there was no cross-check to prevent downscale when active stream counts > 0.
- KV cache warm-up sensitivity: heavy dependencies on locally-cached prefix/KV meant evicted workers experienced many mid-chain cache misses, amplifying latency and fragmentation when clients reconnected.
- Observability blind spot: no high-fidelity pre-downscale playback signal that would predict fragmentation risk (we had stream-frag-rate, but it was not part of autoscaler preflight checks).
- Rollout automation: the rollout job sequentially applied the new config per region without preflight traffic-shape tests for streaming workloads.

What went well (response):
- Alerting: the streaming-frag metric and reconnect-rate alert fired within 3 minutes; oncall was paged and mobilized quickly.
- Rapid rollback: infra team rolled back the canary within 9 minutes of first alerts, which stopped additional downscales.
- Cross-team coordination: runtime, infra, and SRE formed a triage ribbon and executed a targeted hotfix to add 'stream-in-flight' protection within 13 minutes.

What did not go well:
- Canary targeting missed streaming-heavy shards -> we should have traffic-shaped canary to include streaming load classes.
- Autoscaler config lacked a simple guard for 'active streaming sessions' and downscale decisions.
- No documented runbook step for "autoscaler-induced fragmentation" leading to slower decision-making early on.

Immediate mitigation and actions taken during incident:
- Rolled back autoscaler config in EU-west canary pool (03:31 UTC).
- Temporarily disabled the aggressive downscale path globally for v2.7.0 until fix (03:34 UTC).
- Emergency runtime patch: set nodes with stream-in-flight > 0 to be exempt from downscale for the next 120s (03:45 UTC).
- Increased cache preheat during recovery by seeding top prefixes from persistent store for reconnecting sessions in EU-west.

Post-incident follow-ups (action items):
P0 priority (must complete within 1 week):
- Add autoscaler downscale veto when 'stream-in-flight' > 0 at node level (owner: Marco; due: 2029-06-19).
- Rework canary pipeline to ensure canary traffic includes streaming-heavy shards and an explicit streaming stress test step before region rollout (owner: Priya; due: 2029-06-18).
- Add preflight simulation that computes risk score for cache-warmup sensitivity using historical KV eviction metrics (owner: Daniel; due: 2029-06-20).

P1 priority (complete within 30 days):
- Replace the low-CPU+low-TPS downscale gate with a hysteresis-aware model that incorporates persistence of 'stream affinity' and node-leasing state (owner: Infra team; due: 2029-07-10).
- Create a synthetic canary that runs long-lived streaming sessions (5–10m) with induced reconnects to surface fragmentation risk during infra rollouts (owner: SRE tests; due: 2029-07-01).
- Update monitoring to make 'stream-frag-rate' part of autoscaler observability dashboards and preflight gating (owner: Observability; due: 2029-06-22).

Runbook changes (short term):
- New runbook section: "Autoscaler rollout -> streaming risk" with immediate steps: 1) verify canary contains streaming shards, 2) check active stream counts, 3) hold rollout if stream-in-flight > threshold, 4) have rollback playbook pre-queued. (owner: Jules; due: 2029-06-16)
- Add explicit pager for "autoscaler mass downscale" that routes to infra-leads and runtime oncall simultaneously. (owner: SRE paging; due: 2029-06-15)

Engineering fixes (medium term):
- Implement autoscaler veto API so runtime can flag protected sessions or worker processes. (owner: infra + serving-runtime; due: 2029-07-10)
- Improve KV-cache transfer protocol to allow faster warmup on worker replacement (owner: serving-runtime; due: 2029-08-01).

Postmortem notes and hypotheses to validate:
- Hypothesis: downscales were too coarse-grained and evicted entire worker groups simultaneously; test by replaying the canary config in staging with controlled streaming load.
- Hypothesis: reconnect storms were amplified by client libraries that re-attempt aggressively; validate client backoff behavior and consider server-side guidance headers to reduce thundering reconnects.

Customer communication:
- SRE and CS drafted a joint incident summary for affected accounts; outreach prioritized customers with production streaming dependencies. (owner: Customer Success; due: 2029-06-14)

Lessons learned / TL;DR:
- Autoscaler rollouts that change node lifecycle behavior must account for long-lived streaming sessions and local cache dependencies.
- Canary must be representative of workload classes (especially streaming) not just % of traffic.
- Add veto/guard signals from runtime into autoscaler preflight checks to avoid evicting in-flight work.

Appendix: quick recovery commands used during incident (scrubbed):
- rollback command: infra-rollout revert --region eu-west --config autoscaler/v2.6.9
- emergency hotfix: kubectl patch daemonset serving-runtime --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"protect-stream-inflight":"true"}}}}}'

References / links (also listed above):
- Incident ticket: JIRA-INC-4321
- Rollout PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1182
- Runtime guard PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2145
